rawFindings.title: Incorrect tokens identification for arrow spacing
rawFindings.explanation: The original implementation used sourceCode.getTokenBefore(node.body) and moved backward until finding the '=>' punctuator token. The new implementation attempts to get tokens starting from the first token of the node, moving forward to find '=>'. However, it incorrectly initializes and updates the 'before' token without proper handling of initial value, and its logic changes the direction and may cause incorrect tokens referencing, which may lead to incorrect fixing behavior.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original method for getting the arrow token by using sourceCode.getTokenBefore(node.body) and looping backward until the '=>' token is found. Ensure that the 'before' and 'after' tokens correspond to tokens immediately before and after the '=>' token to maintain expected behavior.

The new code instead starts from the first token of the node and moves forward until it finds the '=>' token. This changes the direction of search and also keeps track of the 'before' token as the token before '=>'. This can cause incorrect tokens to be identified for 'before' and 'after' when the arrow function body involves parentheses or complex expressions, p
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert getTokens implementation back to original behavior to reliably get the arrow token by searching backward from node.body token, or carefully test new forward scanning logic to ensure it correctly identifies the tokens before and after the arrow in all edge cases.
